paper_title: A Coin Has Two Sides A Novel Detector-Corrector Framework for Chinese   Spelling Correction
caption: Proportion of correct corrections among various error detection results in SIGHAN15. "P" signifies the errors in high precision results, "R" signifies in high recall results, "N" signifies not been detected. The suffix "W" indicates cases where correction has failed.
model_annotation: The image presents two pie charts, one labeled "All Changes" and the other "All Errors," which appear to illustrate the distribution of various categories related to error detection and correction results in the SIGHAN15 dataset. Each chart is divided into six slices, representing the categories P, PW, R, RW, N, and NW. The "All Changes" chart shows the following proportions: P, light green, 50%; R, beige, 26%; RW, brown, 14%; NW, blue, 5%; PW, dark green, 4%; and N, light blue, 1%. A legend to the right of the charts provides a key to the colors used for each category. The charts do not feature a traditional legend but instead display percentage labels inside or next to each slice; no slices are visually emphasized through explosion, offset, or bolding, and the segments do not appear to be ordered in any specific way beyond their size representation of the proportion.
